summary: Modular monolith architecture: Next.js (web) + React Native with Expo (Android) with Supabase Cloud and Supabase Postgres on Google Cloud Run + Supabase platform (Google Cloud Run in asia-south1, Supabase platform in ap-south-1). Driven mainly by project.type and team.languages; about $140-440/month.

architecture.justification: A marketplace project with a team of 3 benefits from clear module boundaries inside one deployable unit, without the operating cost of separate services.

alternatives.why_not: Needs 12+ people, a devops engineer, 1,000,000+ users and scalability priority 4+; here team.size is 3, team.has_devops is false, scale.users_12_months is 30,000, priorities.scalability is 3, team.experience is intermediate.
No workload is heavy enough to need its own service (realtime under 2,000 concurrent users, no model training, no write-heavy iot, analytics or gaming).
Traffic is steady, so always-on servers are cheaper than pay-per-request.

frontend.justification: Next.js (web) + React Native with Expo (Android): server rendering or pre-built pages serve search engines; suited to project.type marketplace; an 8-week MVP leans on a large library ecosystem; uses javascript, typescript, which the team already writes; handles the 30,000 users expected in 12 months (about 800 concurrent at peak). Web app: Next.js (server rendering, static generation and route handlers in one framework). Android app: React Native with Expo (one TypeScript codebase for Android and iOS).

alternatives.why_not: Next.js (web) + React Native with Expo (Android) is preferred because an 8-week MVP leans on a large library ecosystem.

alternatives.choice: React Native with Expo (one codebase for web and Android)
alternatives.why_not: React Native with Expo (one codebase for web and Android): client-side rendering is weak for search engines.

tradeoffs: Heavier runtime than static generators
Full features are easiest on Vercel; self-hosting needs Node or a container

backend.justification: Supabase Cloud: includes sign-in, file storage, real-time out of the box, so fewer services for a team of 3 to wire up; suited to project.type marketplace; has built-in real-time support; uses javascript, typescript, which the team already writes, for the 8-week MVP; handles the 30,000 users expected in 12 months (about 800 concurrent at peak). Postgres, Auth, Storage, Realtime and Edge Functions behind one dashboard. Deployed in ap-south-1.

alternatives.why_not: Fastify (Node.js) scores 3.8 points higher on its own, but the best full stack built around it totals 14.4 points less once hosting, database and cloud fit are counted.
Next.js route handlers scores about as high on its own, but the best full stack built around it totals 18.4 points less once hosting, database and cloud fit are counted.

Supabase Cloud is preferred because it includes sign-in, file storage, real-time out of the box, so fewer services for a team of 3 to wire up. It would use python, which the team writes, but with its best hosting and database the whole stack totals 22.6 points less.

ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Deployed in ap-south-1.

assumptions: Priced for 30,000 monthly active users (the larger of users_at_launch and users_12_months), interpolated between list-price anchors in the knowledge base.
Prices are list prices of the cheapest region inside the chosen residency zone; taxes are excluded.
Database storage is priced for 50 GB (scale.data_volume_gb_12_months).
A staging environment is added for a team of 3 or more (x1.1 to x1.3 on core services).
The upper bound is limited to 3 times the lower bound: the components do not all peak in the same month, so the band stays within one order of magnitude.
Supabase Postgres: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Supabase platform: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Supabase Auth: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Supabase Realtime: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Supabase Storage: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Supabase Queues (pgmq) and pg_cron: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Firebase Cloud Messaging: free tier used at the low end (FCM is free with no message cap)
Payment gateway fees (about 2% per transaction), one-time costs, domain names and developer seats are not infrastructure and are excluded.

warnings.message: The estimate is $140-440 a month against a budget of $150, so a busy month could go over.
timeline.mvp_weeks is 8 against an estimate of about 10 weeks for the scope.
The CDN (Google Cloud CDN) is used for static assets only; personal data stays at the origin in india.
CERT-In Directions (28 April 2022) require system logs to be kept for 180 days within India and cyber incidents to be reported within 6 hours; set log retention in the India region accordingly.
India DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025: Notice and consent for processing personal data; Data principal rights: access, correction, erasure, grievance redressal. The stack keeps data in ap-south-1.
The low end of the estimate relies on free tiers: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM is free with no message cap). Check them against the expected traffic.

Claim stock, slots or bookings in Supabase Postgres with a single conditional UPDATE (for example WHERE stock > 0) or a row lock inside a transaction, not a read followed by a write, so two buyers cannot take the last unit.

Make every Cashfree Payments charge and refund call idempotent (one idempotency key or order id per attempt) and store processed webhook event ids, so a retry or a repeated webhook never charges or refunds twice.

Card data still falls under PCI DSS even though compliance does not list pci_dss. Use the payment provider's hosted checkout or redirect so card numbers never touch these servers; the merchant then files the short Self-Assessment Questionnaire A instead of a full assessment.
SMS to Indian numbers must go through a DLT-registered sender and templates; register before launch.
